notes: Use-case summary: CX platform for 450 agents, primary value = automated post-call summaries + QA highlight extraction for coaching.
Goal: reduce QA review time by 60% and speed up coaching cycles; routing suggestions for triage agents during spikes.
Workload: 12k calls/month baseline, peak spikes 4-5x during promos (Black Friday-like events). Need graceful degradation not full failure.
Latency targets: agent-assist suggestions <= 250ms ideally, post-call summary available < 30s after call end for supervisor queue.
Throughput target for Dedicated: sustain 95 concurrent transcriptions + 300 concurrent summary jobs during spikes.
Model preferences: open to smaller LLaMA-style variants for assist, prefer Redwood verify low-latency profiles; fallback to cheaper quantized variants during overload.
Data flow: transcripts stored in encrypted bucket -> summarizer -> QA extractor -> coaching dashboard; must support redaction at ingestion and retention controls.
Security asks: SSO/SAML integration, customer-managed KMS, audit logs for all inference requests, retention policy enforcement (90/365 day options).
Quote from CTO during demo: "If we lose summaries for even 10% of peak calls, ops volume doubles. Need deterministic fallbacks."
POC metrics: extractive QA recall 0.78, abstractive summary ROUGE-L 0.64 vs internal gold dataset; latency 180ms median for single-turn assist, 95th=720ms during synthetic spike test.
Key technical blocker: current autoscaler prototype did not bring up extra Dedicated capacity fast enough during 5x spike test - investigating policy tuning.
Integration notes: they use Genesys cloud for telephony, Zendesk for ticket creation; prefer webhook-based tool-calling for 3rd party actions.
SE feedback (Rita): Recommend Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and KV prefix caching to reduce token costs for repetitive agent prompts.
Commercial ask: enterprise SLA with uptime + latency SLOs, monthly committed throughput, and option for VPC Private control plane later.
